C9000083.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 083 (Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions.; papers: A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/083.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_MAIN.statement: Literal thm:main: the uniform short directional Hilbert-transform L2 estimate for every Lipschitz unit field, including uniform inner truncations. Not certified here.

C_BAND_REDUCTION.statement: red:band-implies-main: the band restricted estimate implies thm:main.

C_MODEL_REDUCTION.statement: red:model-suffices: the three finite model estimates imply thm:band-restricted.

C_ORDINARY_MODEL.statement: The ordinary logarithmic-m and scalar reverse-disparity estimates used by assembly:all-model-estimates hold for all finite admissible forms.

C_POPULAR_MODEL.statement: assembly:improved-model and its finite-form transfer: integral_F ||P|| <= L^{-20} N |F| for the popular model.

C_VERTEX.statement: assembly:vertices: the root analytic amplitude has the uniform Lp bound at each shift vertex.

C_PATH_EXPANSION.statement: hier:path-expansion: good terminal paths carry at least half the root amount with the terminal bounds used by the vertex estimate.

C_PATH_PRODUCT.statement: res:path-product and eq:src-22: the top-weighted good active-path product has the stated polynomial bound.

C_INTERPOLATION.statement: assembly:interpolation and the exponent budget yield the central power gain without a K-dependent loss.

C_REASSEMBLY.statement: The fixed and moving exceptional-set estimates control the original P, permitting the averaged original-decomposition argument.

C_TOP_INTERVAL.statement: Assumed analytic input: eq:src-11 bounds every interval-of-lengths top sum by L^{C_top} h_T^8 on Z_0, with the enlargement following eq:src-12.

C_MASS_CAP.statement: Assumed analytic input: eq:src-12 gives n <= N L^{C_n} on Z_0, with positive bounded top weights and the stated parameter bounds.

C_CENTRAL_COEFFICIENT.statement: Positive eligible masses cancel exactly in eq:src-30, including stopping at zero; only boundary ratios remain.

C_BOUNDARY_CORE.statement: For every finite k,r the stopped telescope is exact; geometric layers retain the terminal tail; the potential and normed-vector Abel bounds have no depth factor. Real Lean 4.31.0 compiler certification exists; independent statement-fidelity review is outstanding.

C_BOUNDARY_GRID.statement: For one common uniform translation and the literal masses/stopping levels, expected total boundary log loss is at most 2 epsilon sum_{j<k_T}G^{-j}log(M_j(epsilon)/h_T), hence at most 2 epsilon (1-G^{-k_T})/(1-1/G) log(n/h_T).

C_BOUNDARY_PACKET.statement: Given the top interval bound H_T, the actual stopped central coefficients have expected packet-removal error at most 2 epsilon (mu/K) H_T times the local-mass potential, uniformly in finite depth.

C_BOUNDARY_LOSS.statement: Conditional on the recorded upstream top-interval and mass-cap inputs, the literal expected-error conclusion of assembly:boundary-loss holds for arbitrary finite angular depth, with the original eligible masses and one common translation.
